mainText: Good morning, Landon. Here's your brief for Tuesday, November 24, 2026. Let's start with the markets. Wall Street staged a huge rebound on Monday, snapping a seven-day losing streak for the S&P 500. The S&P 500 jumped 4.7 percent to close at 7,237. The Dow gained about 1,448 points, or 3 percent, to finish at 49,595. And the Nasdaq soared 6.5 percent to 24,090. It was the best day for the major indexes since April of 2025, and it came after a week in which the S&P 500 fell more than 8 percent. The main driver was Nvidia, which surged about 31 percent after its board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive, less than two weeks after he stepped down. Some strategists described the move as a mechanical bounce fueled by short covering and options hedging. On the Fed, traders now see a December interest rate hike as very likely. The CME FedWatch tool shows odds in the low to mid 90 percent range for a quarter point increase at the December 8 and 9 meeting, from the current range of 3.75 to 4 percent. New York Fed President John Williams said Monday that inflation is still too high and that the Fed has work to do to bring it back to its 2 percent goal. He expects inflation to end this year around 3.5 percent. Meanwhile, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said over the weekend that tightening too much could be a policy mistake. Next, more on Nvidia. Along with bringing Huang back, the board said it is creating a new national security and export control committee. The rally added roughly one trillion dollars to Nvidia's market value in a single session. Next, a major cybersecurity deal. CrowdStrike agreed to acquire Zscaler in a deal valued at about 44 billion dollars, which would combine two of the biggest names in the industry. Zscaler shares rose about 13 percent, while CrowdStrike fell nearly 10 percent. And finally, Oatly shares more than doubled at one point on Monday after investment firm Verlinvest raised its stake in the oat milk maker to roughly 43 percent. Oatly's board urged shareholders not to tender their shares into Verlinvest's offer. On the calendar today, the Conference Board releases its November consumer confidence reading at 10 a.m. Eastern. Analog Devices, Best Buy, and Medtronic report before the open, and Dell, Workday, Autodesk, and HP report after the close. Tomorrow brings the October PCE inflation report, a revised look at third quarter GDP, and the Fed's Beige Book. Markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving. Here's your fun fact. In the twin villages of Baarle-Hertog and Baarle-Nassau, the border between Belgium and the Netherlands zigzags through streets, shops, and even living rooms, creating dozens of tiny enclaves. When the line cuts through a house, the location of the front door decides which country the home belongs to. Over the years, some residents have reportedly moved their front doors to switch countries. Have a great day.
